scenes.text: Two hundred twelve days into your watch. The cargo ship Meridian is passing Saturn, and you are the only one awake.
Five crew. Four of them in cryosleep. Your job is simple. Stay awake. Watch the ship. Wake no one.
Earth is nearly nine hundred million miles behind you. A call for help takes eighty minutes to get there. Nobody is coming.
At three in the morning, ship time, the proximity alarm goes off. Something is touching the hull.
It isn't debris. Debris doesn't change direction. This is climbing along the outside of the ship, hand over hand, toward the airlock.
Space is silent. But steel carries sound.
Three slow knocks, on the outer door. Nothing out there should be alive.
You wipe the frost from the glass. A figure in a spacesuit. It lifts one hand, and presses it against the window.
The name tag reads R. Voss, pilot. That is your name.
And the suit's oxygen gauge reads zero.
Your own suit is still hanging in the locker behind you.
Then the radio crackles. And your own voice says: Please. Let me in. I'm the real one.

choice.narration: Do you open the airlock? Or keep it sealed?
choice.question: WHAT DO YOU DO?
